answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with an escalating identity-creation burn: registering an identity burns a small fee, and the fee rises steeply with each extra identity funded from the same source, like a willow branch bending further under every added weight. One honest agent pays almost nothing, but an attacker filling a canyon with thousands of fakes faces a compounding cost, so no bridge of cheap clones can cross it: the hundredth fake costs far more than the first, and the thousandth costs more than the fakes could ever earn.
